Subject: Sudden p95 increase after PSI7 v3 rollout (urgent)

Ben —

We started seeing a marked increase in tail latency (p95) across our endpoints after your recent PSI7 v3 rollout last night. The spike began around 23:40 PT and looks sustained — p95 bumped from ~230ms to ~980ms on our traffic (primarily short chats and small prompt families). This is impacting live customer flows.

Can you advise immediately: is there a known issue with v3? We need an urgent plan — if rollback is available we want it enabled; otherwise we9d like an SLA tolerance or credit while this is investigated.

I can share sample request IDs and traces (attached a short CSV of sample ids). Please loop in engineering and your account contact.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Sudden p95 increase after PSI7 v3 rollout (urgent)

Ben / Alex —

Preliminary triage notes (first 2h):
- Deployed artifact: psi7:v3.1 (rolled at 23:35 PT).
- Symptom: p95 and p99 for short-request class increased ~3.5x. Median unchanged.
- Root signals: kernel-level profiler shows increased memcpy on the attention kernel at sequence lengths <64 for a subset of CUDA kernels we switched to in v3.1; suspect a kernel mismatch for short sequences under our new fused attention path.
- Tenant-specific: FinWave traffic uses shorter context prompts and high concurrency; this surface area is consistent with the perf delta.

Proposed immediate mitigations (fast to implement):
1) Traffic-split: pin FinWave to psi7:v2.9 (previous stable) at the routing plane for 100% while we validate fixes. Estimate ~10-15m to enact with canary guardrails.
2) If rollback is not permitted for contractual reasons, we can pin to psi7-lite (a quantized variant with verified short-sequence perf) and cap concurrency to 75% for 48h while we patch.
3) Longer term: revert kernel selection for short sequences in a targeted patch + rerun perf sweep.

I9m attaching a quick perf pack and a sanitized trace extract for the API IDs Ben forwarded.

Attachments: psi7-perf-graphs.png, trace-extract-20290503.zip

If we get authorization I can run the routing pin immediately and monitor p95.

—Jordan
Lead SRE, Inference Runtime
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
